speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Supported the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill enabling individual commissioners to hold hearings and take private evidence, listed the six commissioners appointed in January led by Justice Peter McClellan, and said the commission's website had received almost 12,000 visits and about 500 calls since mid-January.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Supported the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill, recounted survivor accounts of institutional child sexual abuse including Patricia Feenan's account of her son's abuse by a parish priest, and said Lifeline Canberra had marked its 50th anniversary with calls up 58 per cent over the past year.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Supported the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill with bipartisan backing, named the six commissioners appointed in January including Bob Atkinson, and paid tribute to two Queensland child protection workers killed in a car accident near Townsville while travelling to work.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Closed debate on the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill, said all states had issued complementary letters patent creating a joint royal commission, and said private session participants would not need to testify under oath while identifying details would not be published.

speeches.speaker: Mark Furner
speeches.brief: Three bills—the Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment Bill 2013, the Higher Education Support Amendment (Further Streamlining and Other Measures) Bill 2013, and the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill 2013—were introduced together, with a motion to proceed without formalities and be read a first time agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Jacinta Collins
speeches.brief: A motion was moved and agreed to exempt five bills—including the ACT Self-Government Amendment Bill 2013 and the Higher Education Support Amendment Bill 2013—from certain parliamentary notice periods so they could be considered in the current sitting.

speeches.speaker: Jacinta Collins
speeches.brief: A motion to postpone intervening business until after consideration of the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill 2013 was moved and agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Jason Clare
speeches.brief: Moved government amendments to the Royal Commissions Amendment Bill strengthening confidentiality of private session information, including overriding subpoenas and placing records under a 99 year open access period under the Archives Act.
